frequency_question: What proportion of major economically significant federal rulemakings are successfully carried from proposed rule publication to final rule publication within a 365-day statutory/regulatory timeline?
membership_rule: Includes rules designated as economically significant (requiring OMB/OIRA review under EO 12866), published as a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM), and reaching final publication. Excludes minor technical amendments, interim final rules bypassing NPRM, and rules permanently abandoned before final publication due to scheduling overruns.
coverage_note: 6 named cases representing major administrative hurdles in high-salience domains; estimated population of ~30 comparable accelerated major rulemakings.
known_gaps: Does not account for agency-specific backlogs in non-visa divisions, though DHS/USCIS rulemaking cycles are explicitly represented.
skeleton: Total major rules initiated within a presidential term divided by those completing the NPRM-to-Final-Rule cycle within 12 months.
multiplier: 4 out of 6 tracked historical complex rulemakings successfully completed the full notice-and-comment-to-final-publication cycle within 365 days when pushed on an accelerated internal schedule.
validity_reason: Base rate tied to the standard Administrative Procedure Act (APA) statutory framework and OIRA review timelines, which remain stable across administrations barring major legislative overhauls.
